“Applicable Liquidity Threshold” means $37.5 million; provided
that to the extent that, as of any date of determination, the maximum committed amount of the Super-Senior Revolving Facility (or any Refinancing Indebtedness in respect thereof) is increased in excess of $62.0 million (such excess amount, the
“RCF Increase Amount”), the Applicable Liquidity Threshold shall be increased by an amount equal to 26.0% of the RCF Increase Amount up to a maximum Applicable Liquidity Threshold not to exceed $50.0 million.

full fiscal quarter ending after the Closing Date pursuant to Section 6.01, (A) 8.00% for Term Benchmark Loans, and (B) 7.00% for Base Rate Loans and (ii) thereafter, the following percentages per annum, based upon the Secured Net Leverage

Deterministically-detected quantitative values not covered by any inventory item (MONEY $1.0 million, $3,500, various day-counts, and dates) all originate from cross-referenced Sections 10.07, 6.01, 6.02(1) and 8.01(1) - none of which are part of Section 1.01's own definitional economics (they define assignment mechanics and financial-statement/notice deadlines in other covenants) - and were left un-consumed as genuinely non-operative to the terms being defined here.

Sections 7.03, 7.05 and 7.01 were each confirmed via getReferencedProvision to be independently-operative, substantial covenants (Fundamental Changes, Restricted Payments, Liens) with their own permitted-exceptions frameworks; inlining their full economics into the Asset Sale carve-outs (b), (c) and (r) is out of scope for this single-provision compilation, so those carve-outs are represented as UNSUPPORTED nodes citing the confirmed cross-references rather than guessed or dropped.

The Applicable Rate pricing grid's own boundary language (>1.00, then <1.00 and >0.50, then <0.50) leaves the exact ratio values 1.00x and 0.50x textually uncovered by any tier - this ambiguity originates in the source drafting itself and is preserved literally (via GT comparisons) rather than resolved by the compiler.
